title: Childhood blues and hearing Joe Oliver's band at Tulane gym, 1916
summary: Wiggs recalls the bottle man's blues horn and washwomen, then hearing Joe Oliver in 1916, his opinion of Oliver versus Armstrong and why Oliver's Chicago records pale.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well Dick let me start a little while before Joe Oliver so that you realize why I appreciated Joe Oliver so much. When I was a little boy there used to be a what they called a bottle man going through the streets collecting bottles from children you know the parents would store the bottles in the out rooms and the bottle man would go around and he had a long New Year's Eve noise making horn and in those days they built them pretty well I guess it was about two and a half feet long out of heavy tin as they called it and it had a brass mouthpiece on it well this guy would play the wildest most gorgeous blues I ever heard in my life now of course I didn't you know I didn't know whether anything like that existed before or after he must have gotten right straight from Africa anyway I got those blues and they were perfectly gorgeous to my ear as an eight-year-old boy I got those blues stuck in my ear with the beautiful sounds of the wash women over the washboards so in 1916 when I was exposed to Joe Oliver at Tulane gym after having listened to legitimate music in between my boyhood and semi boyhood 1916 I followed the years I was 16 years old then I heard Joe Oliver's band and that was the cream of the jazz of the world at that time I'm not good at remembering names so well maybe you could mention the names in the band but let me let me say when I heard Joe Oliver I don't near passed out it was just too much for me and and they used a seventh ending sometimes and I don't think I'd ever heard a seventh chord in classical music before then which is considered extremely carny nowadays but when I first heard it in those days you're gonna pick me up with a shovel and that's the way I responded to Joe Oliver and since then I have never heard anybody maybe except Bix who could outdo Joe Oliver now remember that Louis Armstrong will tell you in everything that he wrote that he learned everything he knows from Joe Oliver a lot of people who listen to Joe Oliver's records who were cut in in in Chicago will notice the Joe Oliver pales before Louis Armstrong but something
